counterevidence_considered.description: The analysis derives its sample size from a raw row count (n_units = len(rows)), which would silently inflate n if any crab occupied multiple rows; however, this pathway is closed here because read_trials rejects any input with a repeated crab_id and the supplied file contains no duplicates, so this does not demonstrate the issue.
counterevidence_considered.observed_value: n taken from row count but guarded by uniqueness check

evidence.description: The workflow enforces uniqueness of crab_id at runtime, raising a ValueError if any crab code appears on more than one row, before any statistics are computed.

The reported counts reproduce from the raw rows: 19 tidal and 5 control choices among 24 crabs, and the exact two-sided binomial test against p = 0.5 gives the reported p = 0.006611; the selected result is computed on one independent Bernoulli outcome per crab.

extensions.x-stage1-falsification-attempt: I actively tried to demonstrate the issue by searching for any way a single independent unit could enter the row-independent binomial test more than once: I enumerated all 24 crab_id values in data/input.csv and confirmed they are pairwise distinct (MC01-MC24, each once); I checked the data description for any hint of retesting, split trials, or multi-crab rows and found the opposite is explicitly stated; I traced the workflow to confirm the test statistic (n_tidal out of n_units) counts each row exactly once with no aggregation ambiguity, and that a duplicate crab_id would abort execution before the test runs. I also recomputed the tallies (19/24 tidal, 12F/12M, subgroup splits 8/12 and 11/12) and confirmed they match the report, ruling out hidden double-counting. No route to repeated-unit entry survived these checks.
